tagline: Simplifying the experience of leasing a home and providing accessible rental housing options to the one in three U.S. households who choose to rent.
hero_kpi_rationale: Total property count is the primary driver of recurring revenue and value creation in AMH's business model, reflecting its ability to scale and manage a large portfolio.

kpis.name: Total Single-Family Properties
kpis.explanation: Total number of single-family homes owned by AMH, excluding those held for sale.
kpis.description: As of end-2025, AMH owned 60,337 properties excluding those held for sale, compared to 60,531 in 2024.
kpis.signal: Stable portfolio with modest growth through organic development.

kpis.name: Occupancy Rate
kpis.explanation: Percentage of homes leased during the year.
kpis.description: Occupancy rate declined from 95.1% in 2024 to 94.4% in 2025 (56,756 occupied properties out of 60,337).
kpis.signal: Slight decline in occupancy, indicating a more competitive rental market.

kpis.name: Avg. Monthly Rent
kpis.explanation: Average monthly rent collected per home.
kpis.description: Average realized rent was $2,318 per month in 2025.
kpis.signal: High rents in markets such as Chicago ($2,649) and Salt Lake City ($2,562).

kpis.name: Rent Change on Renewal
kpis.explanation: Average rent increase upon lease renewal.
kpis.description: In 2025, rent increased by an average of 2.5% upon renewal, reflecting the company's ability to adjust rents in a moderate inflation environment.
kpis.signal: Pricing power maintained despite macro pressures.

kpis.name: Joint Venture Properties
kpis.explanation: Number of homes held through unconsolidated joint ventures.
kpis.description: AMH increased its joint venture properties from 3,376 to 3,785 over one year (+409 properties).
kpis.signal: Rapid portfolio growth through strategic partnerships.

kpis.name: Properties Held for Sale
kpis.explanation: Number of homes identified for disposition.
kpis.description: The number of properties held for sale increased from 805 to 1,142 in 2025, reflecting an active asset disposition strategy.

risks.title: Interest Rate and Financing Volatility
risks.score_rationale: The document explicitly mentions capital raising ability and capital structure as key factors affecting results. Macroeconomic uncertainty and housing market adjustments imply increased rate volatility. The Capital category is weighted as a major risk for REITs.

risks.title: Development and Construction Risks
risks.score_rationale: The text details costs, delays, and dependencies (labor, materials) related to property development and renovation. Supply chain disruptions and inflationary pressures are cited as potential impacts. This risk is intrinsic to real estate development activity.

risks.title: Rental Market and Occupancy Fluctuations
risks.score_rationale: The document emphasizes that rental revenues and occupancy levels are affected by macroeconomic and local factors. The decline in occupancy (from 57,486 to 56,756 properties) and high turnover rates indicate pressure in this segment. This risk is central to a rental business.

risks.title: Regulation of Institutional Single-Family Ownership
risks.score_rationale: The text explicitly mentions new laws and regulations aiming to restrict institutional ownership of single-family homes. This is a direct regulatory concern. Severity is moderate as impact is not quantified, but the risk is clearly identified.

risks.title: Property Management and Tenant-Related Risks
risks.score_rationale: Performance depends on tenant quality and internal management via a proprietary platform. Tenant payment defaults and platform efficiency are critical factors. The risk relates to operational management and portfolio quality.

risks.title: Inflationary Pressures and Operating Costs
risks.score_rationale: Inflation is explicitly cited as a factor impacting development, renovation, and maintenance. Operating expenses (taxes, maintenance, insurance) are also mentioned as potentially out of control. This macroeconomic risk directly affects margins.

ai_positioning.summary: AMH does not mention artificial intelligence (AI) or machine learning in its 10-K/20-F filing. The information provided focuses on the company's financial and operational aspects, with no reference to AI or its applications.
